SNUGLITE (blind test): telemetry recovered from orbital physics

Every field below was found without a decoder: candidate byte readings were tested against sunlight, thermal lag, orbital phase, wall-clock time and the IGRF magnetic field computed from the TLE. Names, units and scales are Claude's reading of that evidence, with the satellite name withheld.

Frame type raw:len97

1005 frames, 126 passes, 97-byte payload

A 97-byte beacon frame carrying a large big-endian u32 counter, a GNSS position and velocity block (ECEF and ECI components with 'no fix' values of -1), and a smooth voltage-like value that follows sunlight. It looks like a combined housekeeping and GNSS telemetry frame.

Health. No counter resets in the 16-day window, so no evidence of reboots. The battery voltage sits near 8.1-8.3 V, with a normal sun/shadow swing and no drift in its daily low or high. The data is too short to judge ageing or thermal trends.

battery_voltage [mV]

byte 59 · u2be · sun · power_battery
score 0.86 · ρ sun 0.864 · rough 0.085
raw (or raw*0.001 V) · confidence 0.58

Smooth and narrow (spread 2%), sun-correlated (rho 0.86), 8105-8324 in the 6000-8400 range of a two-cell Li-ion pack. It is higher in sun (8294) than in shadow (8158), with a ratio of 0.983 and a falling trend in shadow (-0.64). That is what a battery voltage does. [3/3 samples agree]

Frame type raw:len214

405 frames, 108 passes, 214-byte payload

A 214-byte housekeeping beacon with uptime and time counters, a GNSS position and velocity block in ECEF/ECI coordinates, solar-panel and power channels that follow sunlight, an attitude quaternion, and a block of temperature-like sensors. Every frame is in sunlight or follows an eclipse by less than 80 minutes, so the lagged correlations are real physics.

Health. No reboots are seen: the uptime counter (158) has no resets in 15.8 days. The battery voltage (59) has a falling daily low of about 15 raw units per 30 days. That is a weak ageing hint, and with only two weeks of data it may be a seasonal effect. Thermal behaviour is regular, with panel temperatures swinging with the orbit, so there is no obvious fault.
